title: ReadWriteConditionalPositions
description: A conditional applicator reached through an in-place one, which is the position issue #174 reports and the one read_write_positions.json cannot express. That document writes its anyOf control on the property ("roViaAnyOf":{"anyOf":[...]}), where readWriteAtLocation sees the applicator and declines to walk it. Here the conditional is on the *object*, inside an allOf branch or behind a $ref, so the allOf merge folds the branch's property schemas into this struct's property map before anything asks about readOnly -- and the answer then came off a branch schema as though the property had been written that way. The merge itself is right and stays: the branch is where the field's type comes from, and without it the value has nowhere to go. What may not follow the property in is the annotation, because a subschema that was not selected contributes none (2020-12 section 7.7.1), and asserting one anyway refuses documents the schema accepts and silently drops values the schema never marked writeOnly. Every RoCond*/WoCond* property below is a spelling of that. The RoBinds*/WoBinds* properties are the other side and are equally the point: $ref and allOf bind on every valid instance, so a fix that stopped reading them would trade a false rejection for a missing check. roBindsBoth and roBindsAllOfAndThen are the sharp cases, one for each place an unconditional contribution can come from -- the parent and an allOf branch -- with a conditional branch naming the same property beside it. A rule keyed on "a conditional mentioned this property" rather than on which schema said what would drop a check the schema states outright. This document used to carry a seventh allOf branch, {"not": {"required": ["roCondNot"], "properties": {"roCondNot": {"type": "string", "readOnly": true}}}}, as the `not` spelling of a property no field is built for. It is gone, and its absence is the point rather than an oversight: a schema whose root carries a `not` in any spelling is compiled to the runtime evaluator and comes out a raw-JSON wrapper with no fields at all (issue #177), so every assertion this fixture makes -- doc comments above tagged fields, a strict read-write key list, a round-trip through a struct -- is about a type the branch stops existing. It only ever coexisted with them because the branch was being dropped unread, which is the defect issue #341 reports; carrying it and keeping this fixture are not both possible. The `not` position now lives in regression/not_in_allof_branch.json, where it is asserted as a verdict on a compiled type rather than as a field that was never built.
